changes.notes: UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy` and work the same way." at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md | Markdown files in .claude/commands/ (older format, still supported) or ~/.claude/commands/ define user slash commands; custom commands have been merged into skills, which support the same frontmatter plus arguments.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "Plugins extend Claude Code with skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers. Plugin marketplaces are catalogs that help you discover and install these extensions without building them yourself." at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/discover-plugins.md | Plugin format uses a .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest; install via `/plugin install <name>@<marketplace>` from the official claude-plugins-official marketplace, the claude-community marketplace, or private/team marketplaces; `--plugin-dir` for local development.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "The sandbox is built into Claude Code and runs on macOS, Linux, and WSL2. Native Windows is not supported." at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md | Built-in Bash sandbox with filesystem and network isolation: Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap + socat (optional seccomp) on Linux/WSL2; configured via /sandbox and sandbox.* settings. Not available on native Windows.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "Claude Code automatically tracks Claude's file edits as you work, allowing you to quickly undo changes and rewind to previous states if anything gets off track." at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing.md | Every user prompt creates a checkpoint; `/rewind` or double Esc opens a menu to restore code, conversation, or both. Caveat: edits made by bash commands or background subagents are not tracked.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "WebFetch takes a URL and a prompt describing what to extract. It fetches the page, converts the response to Markdown when the server returns HTML, and runs the prompt against the content using a small, fast model." at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md | Built-in WebFetch tool with domain-scoped permission rules (WebFetch(domain:example.com)); result is an extraction summary rather than the raw page.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was no): "Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account. The free Claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code access." at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup.md | Requires a paid Claude subscription, a Claude Console account with pre-paid credits, or a third-party cloud provider (Bedrock, Google Cloud Agent Platform, Foundry) billed per token; no free plan or free quota documented.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was partial): "Use the unified PTY-backed exec tool (stable; enabled by default except on Windows)." at https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference | /ps lists background terminals with recent output and /stop cancels them. Background terminals come from the unified_exec tool, which is stable but enabled by default only outside Windows (features.unified_exec), so the rubric counts it as partial.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was partial): "Run tasks in isolated cloud environments, work in parallel, and start work from the web, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, or Slack." at https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud | In-session parallel subagents are stable and on by default (features.multi_agent), which the rubric counts as partial. Codex cloud runs tasks in parallel, but the CLI entry point (codex cloud) is marked experimental, and git worktrees / parallel chats are ChatGPT desktop app features.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "When you run Codex natively on Windows, agent mode uses a Windows sandbox to block filesystem writes outside the working folder and prevent network access without your explicit approval." at https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox | Native PowerShell install (install.ps1) and a native Windows sandbox with elevated/unelevated modes are documented; WSL2 is an alternative. Caveat: unified_exec background terminals are off by default on Windows.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "- **🛡️ Open source**: Apache 2.0 licensed." at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/main/README.md | Source is public at github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli under the Apache License 2.0 (LICENSE file in repo root).

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "The Hobby plan gives you access to Cursor's core features with limited usage. You can use Agent, Chat, and Tab completions with the Auto model." at https://cursor.com/help/account-and-billing/pricing | The free Hobby plan includes Agent with limited usage, restricted to the Auto model; some surfaces such as the JetBrains ACP integration require a paid plan.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "One of the benefits of using custom agents you have defined yourself—or the built-in agents—is that the main Copilot agent can run them as subagents with a separate context window." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/about-custom-agents | Built-in subagents (explore, task, general-purpose, code-review, research, rubber-duck, security-review) plus user-defined custom agents in .github/agents/NAME.md; dispatched via the `task` tool, can run in parallel.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "As Copilot works, Copilot CLI tracks the file changes it makes as it responds to each prompt." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/cancel-and-roll-back | Automatic per-turn file-change tracking with a rewind picker (press Esc twice when idle, or /undo, alias /rewind); choose conversation only or conversation plus files. Works in any directory without Git; not available for remote-backed sessions.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "The --allow-all and --yolo options allow the CLI agent to use all tools, paths, and URLs. You can also set these permissions during an interactive session, by using the /allow-all or /yolo slash commands." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-cli/autopilot | --allow-all / --yolo / --allow-all-tools skip all approvals in interactive or programmatic mode; autopilot mode (--autopilot) adds autonomous continuation; can be disabled by enterprise policy permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "This lets you connect to OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Azure OpenAI, or Anthropic, including locally running models such as Ollama." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-byok-models | COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL / COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE (openai, azure, anthropic) / COPILOT_PROVIDER_API_KEY / COPILOT_MODEL env vars; COPILOT_OFFLINE=true offline mode; BYOK sessions can run without GitHub login.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "You have an API key from a supported LLM provider, or you have a local model running (such as Ollama)." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/use-byok-models | Ollama, vLLM and Foundry Local explicitly documented via the openai provider type; example given for a local Ollama instance at http://localhost:11434 with no API key.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was partial): "This feature is currently in public preview and is subject to change." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/copilot-memory | Copilot Memory is agent-written cross-session memory (repository facts and user preferences Copilot deduces as it works), but it is in public preview, available on paid Copilot plans only, and disabled by default in prompt mode (--enable-memory).

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "The table below provides an overview of differences between plans. All plans include Copilot CLI and Copilot app." at https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/get-started/plans | Copilot Free plan (at no cost, individual developers only) includes Copilot CLI with an AI-credit allowance and auto model selection only; CLI docs also state it is available with all Copilot plans.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "Set reasoning effort level between none|low|medium|high|xhigh (default: medium)" at https://docs.cline.bot/cli/cli-reference.md | CLI `--thinking <level>` flag; CLI README describes configurable thinking budgets per run.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "cline -i "fix the layout issue shown in @./screenshot.png"" at https://docs.cline.bot/usage/cli-overview.md | CLI accepts images via @path mentions; IDE supports drag-and-drop and the + button for images/PDFs. Requires a multimodal model.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "HTTP requests with HTML-to-markdown conversion" at https://docs.cline.bot/tools-reference/all-cline-tools.md | Built-in `fetch_web` tool in ClineCore (called `fetch_web_content` in the SDK); the Adding Context page says Cline will fetch a URL when asked. IDE also has a browser tool.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was partial): "For background tasks, `delegate(..., async: true)` returns a task id, and `load(source: "<task_id>")` waits for the result." at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaif-goose/goose/main/documentation/docs/mcp/summon-mcp.md | Background execution is documented only for subagent delegation via the summon extension (async delegate, `GOOSE_MAX_BACKGROUND_TASKS`); no documented way to background a shell command in the developer shell tool.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "Amp can delegate focused work to specialist subagents. Each subagent has its own context window and access to tools like file editing and terminal commands." at https://ampcode.com/docs/models-and-subagents | Built-in subagents (Search, Oracle, Librarian, Read Thread) run with their own context window and tools; the main agent chooses them automatically or on request, and plugins can define custom subagents exposed as tools.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was partial): "Orbs are remote machines where Amp agents work without using your computer." at https://ampcode.com/docs/orbs | Isolation is provided by running the agent in a remote, metered orb (fresh isolated cloud environment), not by an OS-level sandbox for local shell commands; the Tools page instead recommends a policy plugin or an isolated development environment for untrusted sources.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "Run amp threads continue T-… to attach the CLI to a thread, or pick Copy → Sync CLI Command from the More Actions menu to copy the command with the thread ID filled in." at https://ampcode.com/docs/threads | Any previous thread can be resumed by ID with amp threads continue T-… (also with -x/--stream-json); amp threads list and amp threads search find older threads, and threads open across web, CLI and mobile apps.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "The Dial gives you four built-in modes: low, medium, high, and ultra." at https://ampcode.com/docs/models-and-subagents | Modes route to different models (e.g. GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-5.6 Sol), switched with Ctrl+S or `--mode`; the dial editor lets you pin a specific model per mode for main agent/oracle/subagents, and plugins add custom modes with their own model.

UNVERIFIED on 2026-11-16 (quote not found on page; was yes): "Alt+D toggles reasoning effort for the active model where supported." at https://ampcode.com/docs/cli/keybindings | Alt+D toggles reasoning effort in the CLI; each Dial mode also fixes a reasoning-effort level and custom modes/plugins can set their own.
